# Kitchen Control

> Recipe costing and allergen management software for independent UK kitchens, with near-zero data entry. Scan invoices, ingredient labels and recipes with a phone camera instead of typing them in — food cost, GP%, allergen tracking and PPDS food labelling follow automatically. Built by a working head chef in Mevagissey, Cornwall. From £12.99/month, 30-day free trial (card required at signup).

Kitchen Control helps single-site, independent hospitality businesses cost recipes and dishes accurately (with live GP% tracking), stay compliant with UK allergen law (the Food Information Regulations 2014), and cut kitchen admin time to near zero by scanning supplier invoices and ingredient labels with a phone camera instead of typing them in. "Menu costing" and "recipe costing" are the same underlying job at different scales in Kitchen Control — a menu's cost and GP% roll up automatically from its correctly-costed recipes, with no separate menu-costing exercise required. Kitchen Control also supports importing existing recipes (photographed, or as PDF/Word/Excel/text files) which are automatically parsed into structured, costed recipes, and printing food labels sized for a standard 62mm continuous label roll (Brother QL printers) — including PPDS labels for dishes sold prepacked, compliant with Natasha's Law: full ingredients list in descending order with the 14 regulated allergens emphasised. It is priced and built for independent kitchens and small groups, not large restaurant chains or enterprise hospitality groups.

- [Natasha's Law guide](https://www.kitchen-control.co.uk/guide-natashas-law): what PPDS (prepacked for direct sale) food is, what the label must show, and how Kitchen Control's PPDS Label feature generates it
- [Label printing guide](https://www.kitchen-control.co.uk/guide-label-printing): how Print Label works, label size (100mm x 62mm on a 62mm continuous roll), and recommended Brother QL printers
- [Switching systems guide](https://www.kitchen-control.co.uk/guide-switching-systems): how the Import Data wizard brings in ingredients, yields, recipes and dishes from any spreadsheet, and how to export everything back out
